target: Rank-four string C-group existence for every odd prime power q≡1 (mod 4), q>=5, with group PSU4(q).
source_cutoff: Searches executed through 2026-10-10; indexing and access limitations remain.

queries.query: "On simple groups that admit a string C-group representation" 2026

sources.title: String C-group representations of almost simple groups: a survey
sources.reading_scope: Introduction three general questions; Theorems 3.1, 3.2 and 5.8; Section 5.7 Conjecture 2 and Problem 7. No claim to fresh whole-paper proof audit.
retained_findings: General attainable-rank, maximum-rank and enumeration program.
Conjecture 2 and Problem 7 concern PSL4, not PSU4.
Odd PSU4(q), q>=5, has rank three; corrected rank-three exception PSU4(3).

sources.title: Polytopes of large rank for PSL(4,q)
sources.reading_scope: Fresh primary repository abstract and metadata; exact theorem identifier retained through the primary survey. Not a new complete proof reading.
retained_findings: Every odd PSL4(q) has rank four; even-field PSL4 has no representation. This is not a PSU4 theorem.

sources.title: On simple groups that admit a string C-group representation
sources.publication: The Art of Discrete and Applied Mathematics 9(1), P1.07
sources.reading_scope: Retained author manuscript pages 1–2 including entire Theorem 1.1 and immediately following rank-three statement; fresh indexed primary repository metadata.
sources.access_limit: Direct manuscript URL and ordinary repository detail view returned redirect/access errors; retained primary manuscript and indexed primary print view used. Manuscript itself has placeholder dates.
retained_findings: PSU4(3) and even-field PSU4 have no string C-group at any rank.
Rank-three existence for every odd PSU4(q), q>=5, is an explicitly retained published input.
No rank-four existence or maximum-rank theorem for these latter groups in inspected statement.

sources.title: On the ranks of string C-group representations for symplectic and orthogonal groups
sources.reading_scope: Introduction, Figure 2, Theorem 1.1 and beginning of Section 2. Earlier phase-nine audit also read Section 5; no fresh full-paper audit claimed.
retained_findings: Figure 2 contains no PSU4 rank-four family; this is only historical scope evidence.
Full isometry groups and simple derived subgroups must be distinguished.

sources.title: Rank reduction of string C-group representations
sources.reading_scope: Theorems 1.4 and 4.1, surrounding reflection construction and final discussion, from retained primary text; fresh arXiv metadata.
sources.access_limit: Author PDF URL currently redirects unsuccessfully; saved primary PDF used.
retained_findings: Theorem 4.1 concerns an index-two subgroup of O(d,Fp), p>=5 prime, generated by reflections.
Own inference: in dimension six, projectivization retains a nontrivial determinant character, so it is not the simple PSU4(p).

sources.title: String C-groups with real Schur index 2
sources.reading_scope: First two pages; introduction specifies rank-three unitary constructions and PSU5(3) type {5,5}.
retained_findings: Different solved character-theoretic question, not rank-four PSU4 existence.

sources.title: An Atlas of Polytopes for Small Almost Simple Groups
sources.reading_scope: Scope statement and full unitary table of both author-hosted versions.
retained_findings: Unitary table has no odd PSU4 row; PSU4(5) order exceeds its small-socle scope.
Table absence is not a nonexistence theorem.

sources.title: Unitary Groups and Hermitian Forms, Chapter 9 of Abstract Regular Polytopes
sources.reading_scope: Publisher chapter summary and metadata only.
retained_findings: Concerns finite-dimensional complex Hermitian spaces, not a finite-field PSU4 family.

conclusions.published_small_exception: PSU4(3) has no string C-group at any rank.
conclusions.new_package_scope: Rank four for all odd q≡1 mod4, q>=5; type {4,q²−1,2p} for q>5 and {4,26,10} for q5.
conclusions.maximum_rank_dependency: Separate original phase-nine upper bound; existence alone is insufficient.
conclusions.remaining_scope: No rank-four existence assertion for q≡3 mod4, q>=7; no almost-simple extension classification.
conclusions.recommended_label: Proposed uniform rank-four existence theorem; internally reviewed and computationally certified; priority unverified.

limitations: No exhaustive bibliography or forward-citation search.
One guessed current author-catalogue URL was inaccessible.

Original phase13 mathematical proofs and public files were not edited.
